title: Trump concedes the Iran war cost Republicans the midterms, hours after Vance called it "the reason we lost"
workout: 😴 Rest day — next session Friday. Nothing logged in Hevy yet.

items.headline: Trump concedes the Iran war cost Republicans the midterms, hours after Vance called it "the reason we lost"
Oil collapses 8.7% and the Dow adds 1,569 points as markets price an end to the war
Trybunał Konstytucyjny zwołuje kolejne Zgromadzenie Ogólne na 10 listopada, a minister sprawiedliwości wysyła prezydentowi konstytucję z zaznaczonymi artykułami
Trump called the war's role in the rout "largely true" and Vance repudiated it outright
items.summary: a clean break from the White House line carried yesterday.

items.headline: Brent settled at $94.62 and WTI at $88.12, oil's worst week since April 2020, as the sweep raised the odds of a Hormuz deal
Seoul's KOSPI fell as much as 5.2% and tripped a five-minute sidecar on Samsung and SK Hynix
items.summary: the AI trade, not the election, is now the market's problem.

items.headline: Hormuz talks
items.summary: Qatari mediators still holding a draft; Tehran says there is a "long way to go" and no deal is signed.

items.headline: Israeli coalition
items.summary: Herzog accepted the certified results and opened consultations; Likud and Yashar speak last today.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO
items.summary: roadshow expected the week of 9 November; Opus 5.5 shipped this morning, price range still blank.

items.headline: Trump admits the Iran war sank the Republicans
items.summary: he told Fox the war was "largely true" the reason for the defeat while Vance said it was "the reason we lost"; Schumer replied that the war "must end".
items.matters: a defeated president who agrees with his own party's diagnosis is far likelier to take a deal.

items.headline: Herzog accepts the results and opens coalition talks
items.summary: Israel's president called the certified count legally binding and began meetings with party leaders, with neither Netanyahu's 53 seats nor Eisenkot's 48 enough to govern.
items.matters: the mandate he hands out in the next few days decides whether Netanyahu stays.

items.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to ten more years
items.summary: Hong Kong's High Court imposed the term for colluding with foreign forces, ruling the offence grave; he had been due for release in January and now faces late 2036.
items.matters: the sentence shows Beijing will keep its best-known prisoner past the point where release had become thinkable.

items.headline: Kyiv suffers its worst water outage of the war
items.summary: Russian strikes on energy sites across nine regions cut pumping for more than 24 hours, as the death toll in Komyshuvakha rose to 40.
items.matters: the grid campaign is now aimed at winter habitability, not at front lines.

items.headline: Kenya discharges its first five Ebola patients
items.summary: 46 more contacts left quarantine, taking the total released to 66, with nine cases and two deaths recorded and no new infection since 19 October.
items.matters: the outbreak's end is now a 42-day countdown rather than an active emergency.

items.headline: TK wchodzi w kolejny etap kryzysu
items.summary: sędzia Anna Korwin-Piotrowska zapowiedziała Zgromadzenie Ogólne na 10 listopada, które ma zająć się administrowaniem Trybunałem i sposobem wyznaczania składów.
items.matters: jeśli nowi sędziowie znów zbiorą się bez starych, spór o legalność TK przeniesie się na każde przyszłe orzeczenie.

items.headline: Żurek wysyła konstytucję do kancelarii prezydenta
items.summary: minister sprawiedliwości zapowiedział przekazanie egzemplarza z zaznaczonymi artykułami 10, 126, 173 i 194, mówiąc, że Trybunał to nie stadion.
items.matters: to formalne postawienie prezydenta przed wyborem między podporządkowaniem się TK a dalszą eskalacją.

items.headline: CBA zatrzymało 25 osób w sprawie Ostrołęki
items.summary: wśród zatrzymanych jest, według Radia Zet, Mirosław Kowalik, obecny prezes Westinghouse Polska i były szef Enei; straty szacuje się na 1,35 mld zł.
items.matters: afera z lat 2018-2019 dotyka człowieka prowadzącego negocjacje o elektrownię jądrową.

items.headline: RPP zostawia stopy bez zmian
items.summary: decyzja na listopadowym posiedzeniu utrzymuje dotychczasowy poziom; konferencja Adama Glapińskiego odbywa się po posiedzeniu.
items.matters: przy inflacji po wojnie na Bliskim Wschodzie Rada woli poczekać na skutki spadku ropy.

items.headline: Sejm zaczyna prace nad PIT i CIT
items.summary: dwudniowe posiedzenie obejmie rządowy projekt nowelizacji podatków dochodowych oraz trzy projekty zmian w kodeksie wyborczym.
items.matters: zmiany w kodeksie wyborczym będą testem, czy koalicja ma większość także po kryzysie w TK.

items.headline: Dow jumps 1,569 points on the sweep
items.summary: the index closed up 3.03% at a two-month high while the S&P 500 added 1.58% to 7,688.73 and the Nasdaq 1.44% to 25,736.51.
items.matters: it was the S&P's best day since August, driven by consumer, financial and real-estate names rather than tech.

items.headline: Brent settles 8.7% lower at $94.62
items.summary: WTI fell 8.29% to $88.12, both two-month lows, on expectations that a Democratic Congress will push to end the Iran war.
items.matters: cheaper crude is the fastest route to lower inflation everywhere, Poland included.

items.headline: Chip stocks are the no-show
items.summary: Nvidia slipped 3.2% and CoreWeave 9.9% as investors priced in tougher data-centre rules in states such as Texas, while Asian chip names fell across the board.
items.matters: the AI infrastructure trade is now a policy bet on who wins statehouses.

items.headline: Apple closes above a $5 trillion market cap
items.summary: Microsoft also set a record as the two mega-caps absorbed money rotating out of semiconductors.
items.matters: the market is paying for cash-generative platforms, not for capex-heavy AI bets.

items.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: the company says it leads on agentic coding and knowledge work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.
items.matters: a cheaper frontier model resets the price of every coding agent built on top of it.

items.headline: OpenAI chases about $30bn before Anthropic lists
items.summary: Reuters reports the round could value OpenAI above $1.4 trillion, pitched on $50bn annualised revenue heading to $70bn.
items.matters: two mega-listings inside a month will soak up the same pool of capital.

items.headline: Google backstops TeraWulf's $19bn Anthropic leases
items.summary: three credit support agreements cover 401 MW at the Justified campus in Kentucky, with Google able to assume the leases on a default.
items.matters: hyperscalers are now underwriting their customers' landlords, which moves AI risk onto balance sheets.

items.headline: Anthropic signs its first news licensing deal, with AP
items.summary: Claude gets real-time, attributed AP election data, weeks before the IPO and while copyright suits from music publishers continue.
items.matters: paying for content is cheaper than losing the fair-use argument in court.

items.headline: OpenAI buys Pierre Computer
items.summary: Code Storage and the open-source Trees and Diffs tooling will be folded into Codex, following the Pando source-control project disclosed earlier this week.
items.matters: OpenAI is building the file-and-history layer that makes a coding agent usable on real repositories.

items.headline: Dalamud 15.0.3.9 · .NET 10.0.14 · game build 2026.10.16 · last changelog 20 Oct
Patch 7.58 lands 10 November with same-region matching
items.summary: matchmaking and party recruitment expand from logical to physical data centres for NA and EU, behind 24 hours of maintenance.
items.matters: party-finder assumptions about world boundaries break, and plugin code that resolves worlds may need a second look.

items.headline: Evercold pre-orders are open, early access 19 February 2027
items.summary: early access begins around 01:00 PST that Friday.
items.matters: a February expansion sets the API-break calendar for every plugin you maintain.

items.headline: .NET 8 and .NET 9 reach end of support on 10 November
items.summary: no more servicing or security fixes after that date, while .NET 10 LTS runs to November 2028.
items.matters: anything still targeting net8.0 in a plugin chain stops getting patches this month.

items.headline: .NET 11 RC2 is out ahead of .NET Conf
items.summary: the conference runs 10-13 November with the .NET 11 launch and two community days.
items.matters: the next STS arrives while most of the ecosystem is still finishing its .NET 10 move.

items.headline: Taylor Swift takes a third UK No. 1 single this year
items.summary: Patient Zero debuted at the top and The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore returned to No. 1, her fifth chart double.
items.matters: she is the only artist with three UK No. 1s in 2026, and the reissue model is doing the work.

items.headline: My Chemical Romance get their first UK No. 1 album
items.summary: the 20th-anniversary Black Parade reissue climbs from No. 139 to the top of the US chart and takes the UK for the first time.
items.matters: a 2006 record outselling new releases shows what the reissue market has become.

items.headline: Olivia Rodrigo releases her first Christmas single today
items.summary: take me home (4 christmas) arrives at 17:00 PT with a video featuring Cynthia Nixon, plus a 7-inch on Friday.
items.matters: a holiday single mid-tour is a deliberate chart play, not a side project.

items.headline: Florence + The Machine announce Everybody Scream Tour Live
items.summary: the tour recording arrives on vinyl on 6 November.
items.matters: live albums are becoming the default way to monetise a tour between cycles.

items.headline: Kings of Leon return with O My Beloved on Friday
items.summary: one of a heavy 6 November slate that also includes U2's Carnaval De Luz, Bob Dylan's Rolling Thunder box and Skepta's The Fork and Knife.
items.matters: the Q4 release crunch is compressed into a single Friday, and most of it will be invisible by January.

items.headline: Black Doves returns for season two
items.summary: Keira Knightley's Helen is now the prospective prime minister's wife, with Neve Campbell and Ambika Mod joining, and all episodes are up today.
items.matters: it is the week's one thing genuinely worth watching, and Netflix has already renewed it for a third.

items.headline: North of North is back for season two
items.summary: all eight episodes of the Canadian Arctic comedy stream today.
items.matters: the rare comedy that survived a platform reshuffle with its cast and tone intact.

items.headline: Dutton Ranch will shoot season two in early 2027
items.summary: Kelly Reilly confirmed the start at Paramount's UK upfronts, citing 12.9 million viewers worldwide in week one.
items.matters: Paramount+ is betting its scripted future on the Yellowstone universe for another two years.

items.headline: AMC posts record third-quarter revenue
items.summary: $1.71bn, up 31%, on 52 million US admissions, with The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day on its screens.
items.matters: the exhibition business has stabilised, which decides how long theatrical windows survive.

items.headline: The Angry Birds Movie 3 gets a full trailer
items.summary: Paramount opens it on 23 December with Jason Sudeikis back as Red, and a Sonic cameo in the new spot.
items.matters: the holiday animation slot is a three-way fight and this is the family default.

items.headline: Commission opens a call for evidence on DSA ad repositories
items.summary: technical guidelines will cover how VLOPs and VLOSEs publish ad data, with responses due 2 December.
items.matters: if you serve ads in the EU, the shape of that repository becomes a data-model requirement, not a compliance footnote.

items.headline: Two AI Act deadlines land on 2 December
items.summary: the new prohibitions on non-consensual intimate deepfakes and CSAM apply, and systems already on the market lose their Article 50(2) marking transition.
items.matters: this is the last date this year at which a shipped product can become non-compliant overnight.

items.headline: Council agrees its Digital Omnibus position
items.summary: governments kept a route to legitimate interest for AI training data, added ePrivacy exemptions for audience measurement, and dropped machine-readable privacy signals.
items.matters: the Parliament trilogue now decides whether GDPR consent means anything for tracking.

items.headline: Revised Cloud and AI Development Act draft eases sovereignty rules
items.summary: Ireland's compromise narrows Commission powers, extends migration deadlines and allows some overseas metadata transfers; ministers discuss it on 10 November.
items.matters: public-sector cloud procurement in the EU is being rewritten under you.

items.headline: Disinformation Code plenary takes stock
items.summary: the twelfth plenary covered election risks, crisis response and demonetisation of disinformation actors.
items.matters: code commitments are becoming the de facto checklist for platform risk assessments under Article 34.

items.text: Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 were all idle in midweek and return on Friday 6 November; Ekstraklasa round 14 starts the same day with Motor Lublin v Wisła Płock.

items.headline: The Baltic States Prepare for War
items.summary: Isaac Stanley-Becker spent a month with Lithuanian, Latvian and Estonian units rehearsing the first 72 hours of a Russian attack, and found allies preparing to fight without the United States.
items.matters: it is the most concrete account yet of what Article 5 would actually look like if it were tested.
